skill.name: nla-arbitrate
skill.description: Review NLA escrow fulfillments and submit arbitration decisions with the nla CLI. Supports targeted, all-pending, interactive, and automatic LLM-assisted arbitration.
skill.summary: Arbitrate NLA escrow fulfillment requests with wallet checks, review steps, and on-chain decision submission.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill is not overtly malicious, but it operates a high-impact escrow arbitration CLI. Several Markdown backtick and reconnaissance alerts are false positives, while arbitration commands and secret handling are confirmed risks. Auto mode adds prompt-injection and irreversible on-chain decision exposure.

remediation.issue: Auto arbitration can decide disputes from untrusted escrow text.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before auto mode submits decisions, especially for all pending requests.

remediation.issue: API keys and wallet private keys may be supplied through CLI flags.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or a secure wallet store, and remove examples that pass secrets on the command line.

remediation.issue: Arbitration commands can create permanent on-chain attestations.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run or preview step that shows gas cost, escrow UID, fulfillment UID, and decision before submission.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on an external CLI for sensitive wallet operations.
remediation.suggestion: Keep tool access restricted to Bash(nla:*) and document that no other shell commands are required.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Exposure in Auto Arbitration
semantic_findings.description: Auto mode uses an LLM to judge escrow demand and fulfillment text. Untrusted escrow text could steer the model and affect on-chain decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill says the command displays demand and fulfillment text, then documents LLM auto mode. That creates a clear prompt-injection exposure even without a malicious sample in the file.

semantic_findings.title: Command-Line Secret Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows API keys and private keys through command-line flags. Shell history or process listings can expose these secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly mentions API-key and private-key flags and includes an API-key flag example. The exposure path depends on the local shell and operating system.

semantic_findings.title: Irreversible On-Chain Decisions in Broad Auto Mode
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents automatic arbitration for all pending requests while noting that each decision becomes a permanent on-chain attestation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The impact is clear from permanent attestations and all-pending auto examples. The exact harm depends on escrow value and user confirmation behavior in the CLI.

content.value_statement: Escrow disputes need clear review before funds or attestations move on chain. This skill guides NLA oracle users through pending requests, decisions, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to verify the active NLA wallet before arbitration.
Runs NLA arbitration for one escrow UID or all pending requests.
Supports interactive decisions with approve, reject, and skip choices.
Explains automatic arbitration with the escrow-specified LLM provider and model.
Checks arbitration results with the NLA escrow status command.
limitations: Requires the NLA CLI, a configured wallet, and enough ETH for gas.
Cannot arbitrate escrows where the wallet is not the assigned oracle.
Automatic mode depends on provider API keys and the escrow demand settings.
Does not validate the legal quality of the underlying escrow agreement.

use_cases.title: Review Pending Fulfillments
use_cases.description: Scan pending escrow fulfillments and decide each request through an interactive review flow.

use_cases.title: Decide a Known Escrow
use_cases.description: Open one escrow UID, compare the demand with the fulfillment, and submit an arbitration decision.

use_cases.title: Recover From Oracle Downtime
use_cases.description: Manually process requests when the automated oracle listener is unavailable or paused.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Oracle Wallet
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nla-arbitrate skill to show my NLA wallet address and explain what I should verify before deciding requests.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Escrow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nla-arbitrate for escrow UID <uid>. Walk me through the fulfillment, demand, and an interactive approve or reject decision.

prompt_templates.title: Process All Pending Requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nla-arbitrate to scan all pending requests for my oracle wallet. Let me decide each item interactively and verify the results.

prompt_templates.title: Run Controlled Auto Arbitration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nla-arbitrate with auto mode for a specific escrow UID. Preview risks, required keys, and verification steps before submission.

output_examples.input: User asks to review one escrow UID.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies the wallet, starts interactive arbitration, presents demand and fulfillment, records the decision, and checks escrow status.

output_examples.input: User asks to scan all pending fulfillments.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists eligible pending requests, pauses for each decision, submits selected outcomes, and reports which requests were skipped.

output_examples.input: User asks to use automatic mode.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms key availability, warns about permanent on-chain decisions, runs auto mode for the chosen escrow, and verifies the attestation.

best_practices: Verify the wallet address before every arbitration session.
Use interactive mode for high-value or ambiguous fulfillments.
Record escrow UID, fulfillment UID, decision, and status after submission.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-arbitrate all pending requests without reviewing scope first.
Do not paste private keys or API keys into shared logs.
Do not decide requests when the wallet is not the assigned oracle.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides manual or LLM-assisted arbitration of NLA escrow fulfillments through the NLA CLI.

faq.question: Does it require a wallet?
faq.answer: Yes. The wallet must match the escrow oracle address and hold enough ETH for gas.

faq.question: Can it review every pending request?
faq.answer: Yes. It can scan all pending requests where the configured wallet is the oracle.

faq.question: What is auto mode?
faq.answer: Auto mode asks the LLM provider and model named in the escrow demand to make an arbitration decision.

faq.question: Are decisions reversible?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that each decision becomes a permanent on-chain attestation.

faq.question: Where do API keys come from?
faq.answer: Auto mode uses provider API keys from environment variables or explicit CLI flags.
